name: Scandinavian tiled stove
summary: A tall stove clad in white glazed tiles that stores the heat of a short wood fire in a room. The Swedish kakelugn has thin tiles, a plain white face and a soft frame of mouldings.

philosophy.core_thesis: A white tiled stove is both a machine for heat and a piece of furniture: the glaze reflects the light of a dark northern room.
design_principles: Clad a brick core with flat glazed tiles about 20 cm by 25 cm, and 15 to 20 mm thick.
Make the stove tall and slim, 2 to 3 m high, so that it fits the corner of a room.
Glaze the tiles in a plain white; add a few lines of blue or grey painting for decoration.
Finish the top with a cornice, a crown or an urn, and the base with a plinth.
Cut the flue in long windings of 5 to 8 m, so that the brick stores the heat of the fire.
Use a small iron door and a damper of brass, and keep the metal parts in a simple form.
Mould the cornice and the frames in the same clay, so that the tiles and the mouldings match.
Repeat the neoclassical motifs, the garland, the urn and the fluted column, in low relief.
anti_patterns: Tiles in strong colours and heavy patterns
A cast-iron stove with a thin tile on the face
An open fire with no winding flue in the stove
A thick tile with a rough glaze
Loud baroque scroll work on the face

form.shape: A tall corner stove with a flat white face, a moulded cornice, a crown, an urn or a flame, a small door, and a plinth; and some fireplace and frieze tiles.
form.profile: A narrow, upright body with a slight taper; the cornice and plinth make horizontal shadow lines.
form.foot_and_rim: The stove stands on a plinth tile and ends in a crowned cornice that meets the ceiling line.
form.proportion: Height 2 to 3 m, width about 60 to 80 cm, depth about 50 to 60 cm; each face tile is about 20 cm by 25 cm.
rules: Keep the face plain white and show the joints as thin lines.
Put all ornament in the cornice and the crown.
Match the stove to the proportion of the room: one stove for each room.

bodies.rule: Use a pale earthenware tile with a white glaze, and later a creamware body. Use fired brick for the core. Keep porcelain out: it is too dense for the heat cycles.

methods: pressing the tile in a plaster mould
drying the tile in a rack
building the brick core with winding flues
setting the tiles with a wire and clay mortar
forming.joins: Iron wire and clay hold each tile to the brick core, and a thin joint of clay and sand fills the gaps.
forming.details: A fine crackle in the glaze, thin joints, a tile number on the back and a small iron door with a brass damper.

glaze.pattern: A plain white face with a blue or grey garland, a moulded cornice and a crown, with a little gilding on the best stoves.
glaze.gloss: Soft gloss, about 50 to 75 GU, with a slight crackle.
glaze.wear: The glaze crazes in time with the heat and shows a fine network of lines; the white turns a little cream.

palette.strategy: A white or pale cream face with a little blue, grey or green; a very small amount of gold.

firing.kiln: A coal or wood-fired kiln for the tiles; a stove maker builds the stove on site.
processes: a biscuit firing of the pressed tile
firing.scale: In 1882 one Stockholm factory made 6,400 stoves, and the tiled stove was the usual heater of an urban flat.
firing.signs: A crazed glaze, a number on the back of each tile and a stamp of the factory.

pieces.form: Flat tile of 20 by 25 cm in plain white glaze for the face of a stove
Moulded cornice tile with egg-and-dart relief
Tile with a blue garland for the frame of an opening
Frieze tile with a painted wreath for the crown of a stove

positive: tall slim stove with a cornice and an urn

canonical_works.work: Proposal for an efficient tiled stove
canonical_works.maker: Carl Johan Cronstedt and Fabian Wrede

canonical_works.work: Drawings of tiled stoves for houses

emotion.target_response: A quiet, warm calm: the viewer sees a white stove in a pale room and feels the heat that it holds.

use_cases: a Nordic interior with a white tiled stove
a heater or fireplace brief in white tile
a museum label on Swedish stove tiles
avoid_when: the brief wants a strong colour or pattern
the brief needs an open fire
the brief is for a modern wood stove of steel

modifiers.how: Reduce the tile to 13 cm and paint a small blue picture and a corner motif on each.
Change the face to a hearth tile in inlaid clay in red, buff and black with a Gothic pattern.
